subtopics.title: The Sole Trader and the Elements of the Books

questions.question: For a sole trader, the law and the records treat the owner differently, namely:
options: In law, owner and business are one person; in the records, they are kept separate under the business entity rule
In law they are separate; in the records they are one
Both treat them as separate persons
Both treat them as one person

questions.question: Owner's equity is best described as:
options: The money in the business bank account
The owner's interest — what would remain if assets settled all liabilities
The profit for the current year only

questions.question: The one-breath scheme for sides is:
options: Credit assets and expenses; debit liabilities, equity and income
Debit what grows on the left — assets and expenses; credit what grows on the right — liabilities, equity and income

subtopics.title: The Pipeline Words — Journal to Ledger to Final Accounts

questions.question: The correct order of the recording pipeline is:
options: Ledger, journal, final accounts, trial balance
Journal, ledger, trial balance, final accounts
Trial balance, journal, ledger, final accounts
Journal, trial balance, ledger, final accounts

questions.question: The Trading account and the Profit and Loss account respectively yield:
options: The trial balance, then the statements
Gross profit, then net profit — which transfers to Capital

questions.question: A bulk buyer negotiates a lower price before the sale is recorded. This is:
options: A trade discount — never recorded separately; the reduced price IS the price
A cash discount — recorded as discount allowed
A settlement discount — recorded as discount received

questions.question: A debtor settles an existing account early and is granted a reduction. The business records:
Financial accounting is characterised by:
options: Outside audience, past-looking, GAAP rules, standardised statements
Secret reports for the owner only

questions.question: 'Should the shop open a second branch next year?' is answered by:
options: Managerial accounting — forward-looking, for the owner's eyes only

questions.question: Managerial accounting follows no external rulebook because:
options: The law forbids rules for internal reports
Its only test is usefulness to the manager making the decision

questions.question: Under the perpetual system, every sale records:
options: Only the cost of the goods
The sale at selling price AND cost of sales moving out of Trading Stock, simultaneously
A single entry in the Purchases account

questions.question: Under the periodic system, between stocktakes the records:
options: Are silent about stock — only the count reveals what was sold and remains

questions.question: The account says R52 000 of stock should be on hand; the count finds R50 200. Under the perpetual system this gap:
options: Is a named, visible R1 800 question — theft, breakage or error — demanding investigation
Is added back to Trading Stock

questions.question: Sipho puts R70 000 of savings into the business bank account. This is his:
options: Capital — the contribution into owner's equity

questions.question: The R25 000 loan from his aunt is:
options: A liability — the business owes an outsider

questions.question: At year end, net profit flows into Sipho's Capital account because:
options: The profit belongs to the owner and grows his equity

subtopics.title: The Report Card and the Game Plan

questions.question: The statements Sipho hands the bank are the 'report card' because they:
options: Look backward, follow the standard rules, and serve outsiders
Are written for his eyes only

questions.question: Sipho's kitchen-table scribbles about winter stock are the 'game plan' because they:
options: Look forward, answer only to usefulness, and stay inside the shop
Must be filed with the revenue authority

questions.question: The four pairs that decide every question on this contrast are:
A backpack sells for R450 having cost R270. At the till, the counter records:
options: R450 sale in the sales record AND R270 out of the stock counter as cost of sales

questions.question: The perpetual counter lets Sipho see his gross profit per bag:
options: The moment the sale happens — R180 immediately
Only when the bank statement arrives

questions.question: Without the counter, in the periodic way, the R1 800 of missing bags would:
options: Appear as a named loss immediately
Simply look like they were sold — the loss hides inside the year
Reduce the loan from his aunt
